title: Antibiotic for croup in a child
statement: Children diagnosed with croup were not treated with antibiotics.

plain_summary: Review an antibiotic explicitly supplied to treat a child's diagnosed croup.

medicine_groups.name: Antibiotics
medicine_groups.note: These are Australian examples. Any antibiotic explicitly linked to treatment of the episode counts. Table 1 specifies no route. For croup, exclude eye or ear drops and skin creams or ointments used to treat those sites.

options.words: Croup diagnosed at the treated visit
Croup ruled out at the treated visit

needs_facts.what: Age at antibiotic treatment for croup
needs_facts.meets: Confirm age 29 days through 15 years. Ask for the date of birth or age in days when a whole-year age of zero leaves eligibility unclear.

rule_for_models: Confirm for a child aged 29 days through 15 years when the antibiotic treated croup and croup was diagnosed at that visit. Cite the supply and the episode diagnosis. If the indication is missing at a suspected croup visit, ask the carer what the antibiotic treated at that visit. Report a possible finding only when the record or carer links the supply to croup and the diagnosis or eligible age remains uncertain. Cite the supply. Name "Croup" if the episode diagnosis is missing and "Age at antibiotic treatment for croup" if eligibility is unclear. If age in whole years is zero, ask for age in days or the date of birth when eligibility is unclear. Use an answer only for the visit it describes. Report no finding if croup was ruled out, the antibiotic treated another condition, the supply has no link to croup, or age was outside the range.
cannot_be_seen: Dates alone do not identify the reason for treatment. A dispensing history may omit a complication, an alternative airway diagnosis or another infection.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm the diagnosis at this visit and review whether the antibiotic was for uncomplicated croup, a complication or another infection?
